title: IndiGo Is Building a Widebody Business Class — and It Could Reshape How NRIs Fly to India
excerpt: India's largest airline just teased a dedicated premium cabin for its incoming Airbus A350 fleet. With 60 widebodies on order and long-haul routes to Europe already live, a budget-price business class on NRI corridors is no longer a fantasy.
body:
IndiGo, the airline that built India's largest domestic network on a relentless commitment to no-frills efficiency, just dropped a slide in its latest investor presentation that should make NRI frequent flyers sit up. A dedicated business-class product is "under development" for its incoming Airbus A350-900 fleet, with the first aircraft due in 2027. This move signals a significant shift, potentially offering NRIs a long-awaited, competitive premium option that could redefine their travel choices and expectations for journeys between their adopted homes and India.

The details are deliberately thin — no seat type, no cabin layout, no configuration. While specific configurations remain under wraps, the industry consensus is that a competitive offering will necessitate lie-flat seats, enhanced privacy, and a comprehensive in-flight entertainment system to attract the discerning long-haul traveler. But the signal is unmistakable: India's dominant carrier is done being a domestic shuttle service. It wants the premium long-haul passenger, and it is building the product to get them.

## From IndiGoStretch to True Business Class

IndiGo already operates a premium product called IndiGoStretch on 53 of its A321neo narrowbodies. It offers 38 inches of pitch, five inches of recline, complimentary vegetarian meals, and priority boarding. Respectable for a two-hour Delhi-Mumbai hop, but a far cry from what a business traveler expects on a 10-hour flight to London. For NRIs traveling for business or extended family visits, the current IndiGoStretch, while comfortable for domestic hops, simply doesn't meet the demands of a transatlantic or transcontinental journey, where rest and productivity are paramount. For long-haul routes, passengers expect a truly premium experience: lie-flat beds for restful sleep, direct aisle access for convenience, sophisticated in-flight entertainment, and elevated dining options. This is the standard IndiGo will need to meet to compete effectively.

The airline plans to nearly double the IndiGoStretch fleet to over 100 A321neos, pushing daily premium seat count from 2,800 currently to over 4,300 by March 2027. But the A350 product will be something different entirely — a widebody cabin designed for routes where IndiGo will compete head-to-head with Air India's newly refurbished Airbus A350s, Emirates' flagship service, and the Gulf carriers that currently own the NRI corridor. This means moving beyond basic recline to a fully immersive, comfortable environment.

IndiGo has ordered 60 A350-900s — 30 confirmed in 2024, another 30 firmed up in October 2025. That is not a toe-in-the-water experiment. That is a fleet large enough to serve a dozen long-haul routes simultaneously. This substantial order suggests a strategic intent to not just enter, but significantly impact, the long-haul market, potentially opening up more direct routes to major NRI hubs in North America and Europe, a convenience many have long desired.

## Why NRIs Should Care

For years, the NRI travel experience has been shaped by a small oligopoly. Air India and its Vistara merger offered the only nonstop options on most India-US and India-UK routes. Emirates, Qatar Airways, and Etihad controlled the one-stop market through their Gulf hubs. Competition existed, but it was competition among full-service carriers charging full-service prices. This limited choice often meant higher fares and fewer options for the millions of NRIs traveling for family visits, business, or cultural engagements, making the journey a significant financial and logistical undertaking.
